description: Three fictional educational question/document groups. BM25, dense, and reranker orders are authored to illustrate distinct operations; Hybrid is recomputed by RRF k=60. Neither the authored relevance labels nor the document positions are BEIR SciFact observations or measured cross-encoder results.

scenarios.label: Plants and water
scenarios.question: How do plants get water from the ground?

documents.title: Plant roots
documents.summary: Roots take up water from soil and move it into the plant.

documents.title: Rain gardens
documents.summary: Rain gardens store water above and below the ground.

documents.title: Leaves and sunlight
documents.summary: Leaves use sunlight to make sugars.

documents.title: Water through stems
documents.summary: Water travels inside a plant after its roots absorb it.

documents.title: Flower colors
documents.summary: Pigments help give flowers their many colors.

documents.title: Penguin movement
documents.summary: Penguins cannot fly in the air, even though they are birds.

documents.title: How birds fly
documents.summary: Many bird species can fly by beating their wings.

documents.title: Swimming penguins
documents.summary: Penguins use their wings as flippers to move underwater rather than flying.

documents.title: Flying fish
documents.summary: Flying fish can glide above the sea for short distances.

documents.title: Penguin nesting
documents.summary: Penguins build nests and protect their eggs.

scenarios.label: Moon phases
scenarios.question: Why does the Moon seem to change shape?

documents.title: The phases of the Moon
documents.summary: The Moon's apparent shape changes because we see different amounts of its sunlit half.

documents.title: How big is the Moon?
documents.summary: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite and its size changes very little.

documents.title: Moonlight and orbit
documents.summary: As the Moon travels around Earth, our view of its illuminated side changes.

documents.title: Shapes in a telescope
documents.summary: Telescopes show the shapes of distant stars and objects.

documents.title: Solar and lunar eclipses
documents.summary: An eclipse occurs when celestial bodies block sunlight or cast a shadow.
